chunks: From him (Al-Saffar) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi that he was asked:
About the fasting woman who cooks the pot and tastes the broth while looking at it, he said: There is no objection (to it).
And he was asked about the woman who has a young child and she is fasting, so she chews the bread for him and feeds him, he said: There is no objection to it.
And the bird, if it belongs to her.
ai.seo_question: Does a fasting woman break her fast by tasting soup while cooking or chewing bread to feed her baby?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of tasting food during fasting, distinguishing between mere tasting and actual consumption, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence for maintaining the validity of the fast. It specifically addresses domestic scenarios, such as a woman tasting broth while cooking or chewing bread to feed an infant, ruling that these actions do not invalidate the fast provided the food is swallowed and not spat out. This reflects the practical application of the principle that minor, incidental intake does not break the fast, aligning with the broader Shia legal tradition on 'tasting' (dhawq) versus 'eating' (akl).
